name: MC33078 / MC33079 (low-noise bipolar dual/quad)
tagline: Motorola's low-noise bipolar dual/quad (4.5 nV/√Hz, 16 MHz, 7 V/µs). Musiland used the MC33079 instead of the OP275 in its sound cards, and Soomal credited it with better treble detail.
technology: Bipolar, internally compensated, low-noise voltage-feedback op-amp. MC33078 is the dual and MC33079 the quad. The datasheets specify ±5 V to ±18 V supplies. The polarity of the input pair is unconfirmed. Motorola's SPICE library (MOTOR.LIB) tags the MC33078 model 'PNP Input', but that model is a generic Boyle template with an N-channel JFET input pair, so it is no evidence either way. onsemi lists input bias current as +300 nA, the same sign it gives the NPN-input NE5532, which hints at NPN. This is an unchecked inference. Three makers sell the part under the same number. onsemi's part is Motorola's original design. TI has made its own die since Oct 2004, and a TI engineer believes it is the same die as TI's LM833. ST's version is specified at 15 MHz rather than 16 MHz.
manufacturers: ON Semiconductor / onsemi (Motorola spin-off, 1999; ON-branded MC33078/D from Rev. 1, Feb 2001)
Texas Instruments (second source since Oct 2004; own die, shared with TI LM833 / RC4580 / new NE5532 per TI E2E)

lineage.notes: Designed the MC33078/MC33079 ('DUAL/QUAD LOW NOISE OPERATIONAL AMPLIFIERS'). Motorola-branded datasheet copies survive on futurlec, datasheet4u and datasheetcatalog, but their revision and date were not captured. MOTOR.LIB has generic Boyle macromodels of both parts.

Mirrors confirm these MC33078/D revisions: Rev. 1 (Feb 2001), Rev. 2 (Jan 2002), Rev. 4 (Sep 2003), Rev. 5 (Apr 2005), Rev. 8 (Jan 2009), Rev. 9 (Nov 2011) and Rev. 10 (Jul 2025, current). The NCV33078/NCV33079 automotive parts were added to the title by Rev. 9.

TI's datasheet SLLS633 was first issued in Oct 2004. Rev. A (Feb 2005) is titled MC33078, MC33079. Rev. C (Nov 2006) is still the current revision per ti.com. The enhanced-product datasheet is SLOS495. On E2E (thread 1443925), a TI engineer said the MC33078 and LM833 are believed to be the same die because their specs and graphs are identical. A 2026 E2E thread (1652528) says TI's NE5532, LM833, RC4580 and MC33078 are now all the same die.

An SGS-Thomson-branded datasheet survives on studylib. ST's current datasheet ('Low noise dual operational amplifier', st.com) gives 4.5 nV/√Hz, 15 MHz GBP and 7 V/µs. The different GBP suggests ST's own die (unconfirmed).
UTC MC33078 datasheets are reportedly indexed on alldatasheet and datasheet4u. Not confirmed by web search.

reputation.summary: A budget low-noise bipolar dual/quad whose best-documented enthusiast praise comes from Soomal (China). Musiland dropped its usual OP275 for the MC33079 in the Monitor 03 US and 03 PS (PCM1798, 2011). It then used the part in the 06 MX (a TI part, 2013), the Monitor 10 (MC33079DG after an AK4490, 2016) and the 06 Plus (onsemi MC33079DG as a balanced I/V stage after an ES9028Q2M, 2017). Soomal said the 03 US had 'better treble detail' than the OP275-based 02 US. It heard the 03 PS as a little brighter, with finer resolution and better HF transients, but called the gain incremental. Both are whole-product judgements. In the 06 MX review Soomal also said the op-amp was not a top-tier Hi-Fi part. One EDAboard thread weighs it as a TL074 upgrade, and a guitar-pedal swap table says the TI MC33078 has 'very nice highs'. No ASR, Samuel Groner or Douglas Self measurements were found.
sonic_descriptors: better treble detail (Soomal, Monitor 03 US vs OP275-based 02 US; product-level)
a little brighter than the OP275-based 01 PS (Soomal, 03 PS; product-level)
finer resolution, clearly improved HF transients (Soomal, 03 PS; product-level)
'very nice highs' (guitar-pedal op-amp swap table, TI MC33078; folklore)
clean, slightly bright (op-amp-roller folklore; no source found)
typical_uses: I/V stage for differential current-output DACs (PCM1798 in Musiland Monitor 03 US / 03 PS / 06 MX)
balanced I/V stage after an ESS ES9028Q2M (Musiland Monitor 06 Plus, onsemi MC33079DG)
post-DAC filter/gain stage (Musiland Monitor 10 with AK4490)
headphone-amp gain stage (Soomal 'E-brand F-type' headphone amp, MC33078, 2010)
general consumer/pro audio preamps, active filters, guitar pedals, and op-amp rolling in place of TL07x/NE5532
caveats: Needs at least ±5 V (10 V total), so it does not suit low-voltage or USB-bus designs without a boost converter.
Bipolar input with about 300 nA typ bias current, so source impedances and DC paths matter.

TI's MC33078 is TI's own die. A TI engineer believes it is the same die as TI's LM833, and TI now says it shares one die with the NE5532, LM833 and RC4580 (E2E, 2026). TI and onsemi parts may therefore sound or measure differently despite the same number.
Several makers (onsemi, TI, ST, UTC) sell parts under the same number, and ST specifies 15 MHz GBW against 16 MHz for the others. No ON-vs-TI-vs-ST listening or measurement comparison was found.
All the Soomal praise is whole-product judgement, and Soomal itself called the MC33079 not a top-tier Hi-Fi part. Brand attribution in reviews is loose: Soomal called an onsemi MC33079DG 'Motorola'.

silicon_changes.when: Process-migration PCN 20231114002.1 dated 15 Nov 2023; search summaries say it lists MC33078DR. TI confirmed the die merge on E2E (thread 1652528) in 2026. Hackaday covered it on 3 Jun 2026 and Headphonesty in Jul 2026. It is linked to the NE5532 re-spec (SLOS075K, Dec 2025).
part_numbers_affected: MC33078D, MC33078P, MC33078DGKR, MC33078DGKT (other TI MC33078 orderables; covered by the E2E die-merge statement, PCN listing not seen)
silicon_changes.identification: There is no MC33078-specific marker. TI's datasheet is still SLLS633C (Oct 2004, revised Nov 2006), and no MC33078 datasheet PCN was found. PCN 20231114002.1 lists MC33078DR, so TI date codes from 2024 on are probably new silicon (inference). TI's current MC33078 page covers only the dual. onsemi, ST, UTC and Motorola-marked MC33078/MC33079 and NCV parts are not affected.
silicon_changes.summary: TI E2E thread 1652528 ('NE5532, LM833, RC4580 and MC33078 all now the same die') reports that TI unified the four dies while keeping the part numbers. Search summaries describe the NE5532 moving onto the MC33078/RC4580-class die, and Hackaday quotes Rich Cabot identifying it as an RC4580. TI's MC33078DR went through the same November 2023 process-migration PCN (SFAB 150 mm to RFAB) as NE5532DR and LM833DR, so TI MC33078 silicon was at least re-fabricated on a new process. In the earlier E2E thread 1443925 a TI engineer already believed MC33078 and LM833 were the same die. TI's MC33078 may therefore be close to the donor design, and whether its circuit changed is unconfirmed. Its datasheet limits are unchanged.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: Probably small if TI's MC33078 was already the donor design: SLLS633C still specifies 7 V/µs and 4.5 nV/√Hz. The large deltas (slew 9 to 5 V/µs, input diodes removed, ±22 to ±18 V) are documented for NE5532, not MC33078. Behaviour may differ from the Motorola/onsemi-lineage MC33078 that audio users know.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: medium - pin-compatible and SLLS633C limits unchanged, but a process migration is confirmed by PCN and TI says the die is now shared with RC4580, NE5532 and LM833. Re-qualify new TI lots where a design depends on undocumented behaviour such as overload recovery, input protection or capacitive-load stability.
silicon_changes.verification: Merged the two TI-merge entries (research pass plus completeness sweep). Searched PCN 20231114002 with MC33078DR: results list MC33078DR in the PCN. Searched the TI MC33078 datasheet: still SLLS633C (revised Nov 2006), no datasheet PCN found. The E2E 1652528 title was confirmed. An MC33078-level circuit change is still unconfirmed.

silicon_changes.vendor: Texas Instruments and STMicroelectronics vs onsemi (Motorola original design)

silicon_changes.identification: Check the logo and top mark (TI's mark is reportedly 'M33078'); onsemi and ST parts carry their own logos. ST datasheets give 15 MHz GBP, while onsemi and TI give 16 MHz. TI's quad MC33079 appears only in an early TI 'MC33078, MC33079 (Rev. A)' datasheet, and TI's current product line lists only the MC33078.
silicon_changes.summary: The same part number is built on different vendors' silicon. TI's MC33078 is a TI second-source die that a TI engineer believes is identical to TI's LM833 (E2E 1443925); it is now also the shared NE5532/LM833/RC4580 die (see the TI die-redesign entry). onsemi continues Motorola's original design. ST's MC33078/MC33079 have a different GBP specification, which suggests an independent die. No vendor-to-vendor measurement comparison was found.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: Unknown. The headline noise and slew figures match (4.5 nV/√Hz, 7 V/µs), but the internal circuits may differ, so a review of one vendor's part may not carry over to another's.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low - pinout and headline specs match. Differences are second-order (GBW, possibly input stage and protection).
silicon_changes.verification: Searched for a TI MC33079. Found ST's MC33079 datasheet (15 MHz GBP, 4.5 nV/√Hz, 7 V/µs) and an early TI 'MC33078, MC33079 (Rev. A)' datasheet, and removed 'MC33079 (TI)' as a current part. The 'M33078' top mark was not checked.

silicon_changes.when: Initial PCN 11528 issued 19 July 2001. A companion discontinuance notice, PCN 11785, was issued 27 September 2001 for the BMC products that were not transferred.
silicon_changes.identification: No marking rule was found. Motorola/ON parts with pre-2001/2002 date codes would carry Mesa BMC wafers and later ones Roznov wafers (inference).
silicon_changes.summary: ON Semiconductor PCN 11528 announced the transfer and qualification of devices made in the Motorola BMC wafer fab in Mesa, AZ to ON's Tesla wafer fab in Roznov, Czech Republic, which became the primary fab. MC33078D/P are listed, and MC33079D/P are listed per the completeness sweep. BMC products that were not transferred went end-of-life under PCN 11785. This is a same-part-number fab move of the original Motorola MC33078/MC33079 die, separate from the TI-versus-onsemi second-source difference.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: None documented. The same design moved to another fab, and no before/after noise or THD comparison was found.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low - same design and part numbers; any difference would be process spread within datasheet limits.
silicon_changes.verification: Search confirmed PCN 11528 (issued 19 July 2001) and that it lists MC33078D and MC33078P for transfer to the Tesla fab in Roznov, and confirmed that PCN 11785 (27 Sep 2001) is a product discontinuance. MC33079D/P inclusion was not separately seen.

counterfeit_notes: No MC33078/MC33079-specific counterfeit reports were found. Unbranded marketplace lots are the usual risk, for example eBay listings of '50/10 pcs MC33078DR SOP-8 MC33078D' with no maker stated. Alldatasheet gives the TI top mark as 'M33078' (not re-confirmed); the onsemi and ST markings were not captured. Folklore prefers Motorola-marked parts, so relabelled 'Motorola' vintage parts are plausible. Treat 'Motorola' parts with date codes well after 2001, when ON-branded MC33078/D Rev. 1 appeared, with suspicion. Buy from authorized distributors and check the logo, date code and marking.
alternatives: onsemi MC33078/MC33079 (the Motorola-lineage design, not part of TI's die unification)
ST MC33078 (another non-TI source; specified at 15 MHz GBW)
TI LM833 (TI staff believe it is the same die as TI MC33078)

refuted_claims: 'Rev. 4 (Sep 2003) is the oldest ON revision found' is refuted. Rev. 1 (Feb 2001, Reichelt) and Rev. 2 (Jan 2002, Intusoft) exist.

'TI moved the MC33078 onto the same die as its NE5532 in 2024-25' is refuted as a timing and direction claim. The TI E2E die-unification thread and the Hackaday/Headphonesty coverage date from 2026. Search summaries describe the NE5532 moving onto the MC33078/RC4580-class die, and a TI engineer already believed the MC33078 and LM833 were the same die in an earlier thread (1443925).

[change register] 'MC33079 (TI)' removed from the second-source entry's affected parts. TI's current MC33078 product and datasheet (SLLS633C) cover only the dual; a TI MC33079 appears only in an early 'MC33078, MC33079 (Rev. A)' datasheet.
[change register] The completeness-sweep duplicate of the TI die-merge event was merged into the TI die-redesign entry (not refuted).
corrections: Silicon change re-framed. The TI die unification is confirmed by E2E thread 1652528, so confidence rose to medium. Added the E2E 1443925 and Headphonesty sources.

revision_chain_notes:
Motorola MC33078/D: Rev 0 (1996) is now identified from the futurlec copy ('(c) Motorola, Inc. 1996, Rev 0'). Several more Motorola-branded copies were found (rf-microwave.com PDF, datasheet39 ID 467372, datasheet.company freescale.com path), but none shows its revision. MISSING: any Motorola edition after Rev 0 (1997-1999) and pre-1996 data-book editions.

onsemi MC33078/D: Rev 1 (Feb 2001) -> Rev 2 (Jan 2002) -> [Rev 3 MISSING] -> Rev 4 (Sep 2003) -> Rev 5 (Apr 2005) -> [Rev 6, Rev 7 MISSING, about 2005-2008] -> Rev 8 (Jan 2009) -> Rev 9 (Nov 2011, NCV parts added) -> Rev 10 (Jul 2025, current). The http://www.onsemi.com/pub/Collateral/MC33078-D.PDF copy now uses the 'DATA SHEET www.onsemi.com' template, so it serves Rev 10 content. The already-listed https pub/Collateral entry is therefore probably Rev 10 too. Several copies without NCV in the title (yumpu, Rubix, datasheet4u 1495630, datasheetcatalog MC33078-D, alldatasheet 12018) are candidates for the missing Rev 3, 6 or 7, but none shows its revision.

TI SLLS633: original (Oct 2004) -> A (Feb 2005) -> [B MISSING: date and copy not found] -> C (Nov 2006, current). No copy showing the original or Rev B header surfaced. RadioLocman di=224647 (a different ID from the listed di=303635) and alldatasheet 1809749 are new TI copies with the revision not shown. SLOS495 (MC33078-EP): original about Oct 2006; later revisions unknown.

ST MC33078: identified as DocID 2177, with Rev 6 dated November 2012 (current; MC33078YDT qualified status updated, minor corrections). MISSING: Revs 1-5 and their dates, and the SGS-Thomson-era edition date. Candidates: alldatasheet 23287/23288/23289/23290 and the studylib SGS-Thomson copy.

UTC: nothing new.
